subject: memory error if vari ctor throws

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: memory error if vari ctor throws
parts:
I tracked down the problem with log1m() when the argument
is greater than 1.

This unit test:

TEST(AgradRev,log1mErr) {
AVAR a = 10;
AVAR f = log1m(a);
}

causes this error:

Running main() from gtest_main.cc
[==========] Running 2 tests from 1 test case.
[----------] Global test environment set-up.
[----------] 2 tests from AgradRev
[ RUN ] AgradRev.log1m
[ OK ] AgradRev.log1m (0 ms)
[ RUN ] AgradRev.log1mErr
log1m(84891) malloc: *** error for object 0x7fb3d1003218: pointer being freed was not allocated
*** set a breakpoint in malloc_error_break to debug
make: *** [test/agrad/rev/log1m] Abort trap: 6

The root cause is that the constructor for log1m_vari(vari*)
throws an exception if the argument has value >= 1. So I'm
pretty sure we've had this problem all along but haven't
stumbled across it.

I'm going to clean up the other vari classes that do this,
too so that the calling function throws rather than the
vari construtor.

I'd like to know what's causing the problem --- it's not in
the destructors, so I'm thinking it must be in the way we
allocate/deallocate the memory stacks.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: memory error if vari ctor throws
parts:
Thanks.

Sorry for being so dense here, but I don't know how to
interpret that dump.

For one thing, log1m_vari instances should be smaller
than 80 bytes. Is this multiple ones? Or an attempt to
deallocate something from our var stack that's not there?

Here's the vari:

class log1m_vari : public op_v_vari {
public:
log1m_vari(vari* avi) :
op_v_vari(stan::math::log1p(-avi->val_),avi) {
}
void chain() {
avi_->adj_ += adj_ / (avi_->val_ - 1);
}
};
}

and here's the function getting called to create it:

inline var log1m(const stan::agrad::var& a) {
return var(new log1m_vari(a.vi_));
}

What happens is that the constructor for log1m_vari() throws
an exception.

What I want to understand is what's trying to deallocate.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: memory error if vari ctor throws
parts:
On Saturday, May 11, 2013 8:39:57 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
For one thing, log1m_vari instances should be smaller
than 80 bytes.  Is this multiple ones?  Or an attempt to
deallocate something from our var stack that's not there?

I don't know what is up with the 80 bytes thing. It does say that it is trying to free something that hasn't been malloc()-ed. My guess is that the exception precludes the constructor from finishing and then something comes along and tries to free something that would exist if x < 1.

Ben

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: memory error if vari ctor throws
parts: I guess when the "new" in the following code fails (throw an exception), according to here (http://www.parashift.com/c++-faq-lite/memory-pools.html), the compiler generates some code to delete the pointer that is supposed to point to the object we are trying to create.   And this delete is problematic here.

inline var log1m(const stan::agrad::var& a) {
      return var(new log1m_vari(a.vi_));
    }

So if I overload the delete operator with a no-op for this class, at least the test can finish.

@@ -19,6 +19,7 @@ namespace stan {

void chain() {
           avi_->adj_ += adj_ / (avi_->val_ - 1);
         }

+        void operator delete(void* p) {} 
       };
     }
